models_evaluated: Pediatric hypertension clinical decision support (CDS) tool

links.outcome: BP remeasurement and hypertension recognition, high- vs low-intensity implementation support
links.effect: High-intensity (in-person/online training, monthly check-ins, feedback) vs low-intensity (online training only): remeasurement 51.5% vs 23.6%, aOR 3.45 (1.88-6.33); recognition 42.8% vs 24.5%, aOR 2.31 (1.08-4.98).
links.quote: High-intensity implementation was more effective than low-intensity implementation for repeat BP measurement (aOR 3.45; 1.88-6.33) and hypertension recognition (aOR 2.31; 1.08-4.98).

models_evaluated: Pediatric hypertension clinical decision support (CDS) tool

links.outcome: Elevated BP remeasurement and clinical recognition of hypertension
links.effect: Among 9155 elevated-BP patients and 578 incident-hypertension patients, CDS versus usual care: remeasurement aOR 8.70; 95% CI 5.68-13.3; hypertension recognition aOR 2.94; 1.00-8.60.
links.quote: Patients attending high or low-intensity CDS clinics were more likely than those at UC to have elevated BP remeasured (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.70; 95% CI 5.68-13.3) and to have their hypertension clinically recognized (aOR 2.94; 1.00-8.60).

links.outcome: Repeat BP measurement and hypertension recognition by implementation intensity
links.effect: In-person and online training plus monthly check-ins and feedback versus online-only training: repeat BP measurement aOR 3.45; 1.88-6.33; hypertension recognition aOR 2.31; 1.08-4.98. Training effects were not isolated from implementation support.
links.quote: High-intensity implementation was more effective than low-intensity implementation for repeat BP measurement (aOR 3.45; 1.88-6.33) and hypertension recognition (aOR 2.31; 1.08-4.98).

links.effect: High-intensity implementation with monthly check-ins was more effective than low-intensity for repeat BP measurement (aOR 3.45) and recognition (aOR 2.31).
links.quote: High-intensity implementation was more effective than low-intensity implementation for repeat BP measurement (aOR 3.45; 1.88-6.33) and hypertension recognition (aOR 2.31; 1.08-4.98).
